entries.topic: Egri Bikavér: at least four varieties, not three
entries.claim: The Eger record (summary, made.winemaking, law.classification, law.tiers Classicus, exam[0], cards[0].b) and the Hungary country record (exam[1], question r-1ozia0r0) say Egri Bikavér is a blend of at least three varieties, and the country question says the same of Szekszárdi Bikavér.
entries.finding: The Egri Bikavér product specification that applies to wines marketed from the 2023/2024 wine year asks for at least four varieties, each above 5 per cent of the blend, with Kékfrankos at 30 to 65 per cent and the largest share; the earlier Eger texts asked for more, not fewer (five varieties in the upper tiers of the text applicable from 2012, struck to four in a later draft), and three is the count of older rules (a Szekszárd text of 2009 still wrote three), not of either specification in force. The Szekszárd specification, fourth version, applicable from 15 March 2024, also asks for at least four varieties, with Kékfrankos at 45 per cent or more and Kadarka at 5 per cent or more. The national wine body's own pages and the 2024 Hungarian Wine Summit material give the same: four grapes, Kékfrankos 30 to 65 per cent at Eger. The oak minimums the record gives (six months for Classicus, twelve for Superior and Grand Superior) hold.

entries.why: Three is the count of a superseded rule: both Bikavér specifications in force ask for four, so every line that teaches three is wrong for the exam and for a guest.

entries.topic: Egri Bikavér: no fifty per cent ceiling on Kékfrankos
entries.claim: Question c-98c4i3oo (rewrite/categories/r2_hungary_greece.py) keys the ceiling on any one variety in Egri Bikavér at fifty per cent and says the upper tiers ask for more varieties; the Advanced answer a-ih3g5con says no single variety above 50% and Superior requires five varieties.
entries.finding: The Egri Bikavér specification for wines marketed from the 2023/2024 wine year lets Kékfrankos run from 30 to 65 per cent and requires it to be the largest share, so the ceiling on any one grape is Kékfrankos's 65 per cent; the national wine body gives the same band. The fifty per cent band and the five variety rule belong to earlier versions of the Eger specification (the 2012 text), and the summaries of the current text read here give four varieties for every tier, while trade summaries still repeat five for Superior: the count of varieties above the base is not settled by what was read, so the lines drop it rather than give a new one.

Above the everyday version sit stricter tiers asking for more varieties, lower yields and, at the top, fruit from one named site.
targets.new: The ceiling is Kekfrankos's, which must also be the largest share, and with three more varieties required beside it the cap makes the wine a blend by construction rather than by custom, which is the whole point of a name that has been sold as a blend for well over a century. Above the everyday version sit stricter tiers asking for lower yields, longer ageing and, at the top, fruit from one named site.
